messages:
Maya (AE): Heads-up: ACME's security team flagged a production blocker during the POC. Streaming calls from inside their corp network intermittently drop with TLS errors. Can SE/Eng triage?

Sam (Customer Eng): Repro in our lab when traffic goes via their corporate proxy. Error from app logs: 
```
Error: socket hang up
    at afterWriteDispatched (internal/stream_base_commons.js:188:25)
    at Socket._destroy (net.js:444:8)
    at Socket.end (net.js:645:10)
```
Proxy also logs TLS alert: `unexpected_message`. Outside the proxy (home network) streams are fine.

Priya (SE): thanks. Which SDKs did they exercise? Are they using our Node TS SDK streaming over HTTP/2 or a Python HTTP/1.1 chunked flow? Any HTTP_PROXY envs in their app?

Sam (Customer Eng): they tested Node 18 + our TS SDK (http2 streaming) and a Python test harness using httpx (h2). Both fail only when routed via the corp appliance. They provided a corporate PAC and use a forwarding proxy.

Alec (Eng): this smells like a TLS middlebox doing MITM/inspection or an inline appliance that doesn't like long-lived h2 streams. Two quick experiments to isolate: force client to prefer HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming; and enable more frequent TCP keepalives so the appliance doesn't drop idle connections. Also check for proxy rewriting `Connection` headers.

Devon (Infra): can someone post a minimal repro? Also collect SDK debug logs. For Node try: 
```
const https = require('https');
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 3000 });
fetch(streamUrl, { agent, method: 'POST', headers: { 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked' } });
```
Run with `NODE_DEBUG=http2,tls` to dump handshake frames.

Sam (Customer Eng): sharing their sample and a snippet of the proxy alert. Also noting the app sees transient 429s when our client retries, which complicates the trace.

Jin (Solutions): security Q from ACME: if we recommend bypassing the proxy in prod, what are the compliance/pricing implications? They want documented options to present to their security board.

Maya (AE): they also want an estimate for Dedicated/private (VPC) onboarding time and any additional monthly costs if we recommend that to avoid proxy.

Priya (SE): quick answers: Dedicated (private) avoids corp proxy if we peer into their VPC or use customer-managed egress; typical onboarding is 3-6 weeks depending on network approvals. Pricing: baseline includes reserved capacity cost + infra premium; I'll paste the pricing sheet.

Alec (Eng): back to triage: if the pcap shows TLS `unexpected_message`, that's a middlebox issue. Short-term engineering workarounds for the POC: 
- preferHttp1 toggle in SDK to force chunked HTTP/1.1 streaming
- lower TCP keepalive interval and enable probe counts (to keep connection alive through inspection windows)
- add a debug flag to disable TLS session tickets (not for prod) to see if session resumption is tripping the appliance
- implement smaller write sizes to avoid large TLS records that break some appliances

Devon (Infra): please capture a pcap at the app side and the proxy if possible. Look for TLS Alert length and `unexpected_message` source. Also confirm whether the proxy rewrites SNI or injects enterprise cert.

Sam (Customer Eng): customer tried `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` during debugging and still got resets, so certificate validation isn't the immediate cause. They can run curl through the proxy for a quick lab: 
```
curl -v --http2 --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream" --data-binary @payload.bin
```
I'll ask them to share pcap.

Jin (Solutions): on the security questionnaire: note we support Dedicated/private deployments and certificate/key management via customer KMS. I'll draft the language for the questionnaire saying: "Alternate connectivity options: Dedicated private deployment with customer-controlled egress (VPC peering, VPN) available; typical lead time 3-6 weeks; additional contract for reserved capacity."

Maya (AE): include a short pricing delta estimate for the customer to show budget owners.

Priya (SE): I'll produce two quick samples by EOD: Node + Python. They will include toggles for: `preferHttp1`, `requestTimeoutMs`, `maxRetries` (exp backoff + jitter), `socketKeepAliveMs`, `debugDisableSessionTickets`, and `maxWriteChunkBytes` (to control TLS record sizes).

Alec (Eng): I'll add a small helper script to run `curl` through the proxy and gather a pcap: `scripts/proxy-pcap.sh` (example will be in the POC ticket). Also include `NODE_DEBUG` instructions.

Sam (Customer Eng): action items checklist for our side: 
- run the Node sample with `preferHttp1=true` and report success/failure
- run curl script via corp-proxy and upload pcap
- forward security questionnaire language from Jin
- confirm if ACME can allowlist our endpoints for TCP passthrough (temporary)

poc-bot: created POC ticket POC-4780, assigned to Priya (SE) and Alec (Eng).

Devon (Infra): small FYI: if their proxy uses HTTP CONNECT for tunneling, ensure CONNECT is used for TLS passthrough. If the proxy terminates TLS, Dedicated is the clean option.

Maya (AE): timeline: Priya/Alec samples EOD, Jin questionnaire language in 24h, Maya to follow up with pricing and Dedicated onboarding doc.

Sam (Customer Eng): ack. Will get first pcap and test results back within 24h and post here.

Priya (SE): reminder: do not recommend `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` in production. We'll provide debug-only steps for cert troubleshooting.

Maya (AE): great work team. Keep this thread updated and escalate to solutions if pcap shows proxy-level TLS alerts.
